text: Churned like any cream, but the whey cream is thinner and saltier, so the butter has its own flavour. No churning temperatures were found in a source I opened.

links.name: Tetra Pak Dairy Processing Handbook, ch. 18 Milk and whey fractionation

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: Pasteurised at anything from 63 °C for 30 min to 110 °C for a few seconds, depending on the cream.
Cooled and held for several hours before churning.
Warmed for at least 2 to 4 hours, then cooled gradually to 6–8 °C, to set the fat.
Whey cream from copper vats oxidises faster, so its butter keeps for a shorter time.

links.name: Tetra Pak Dairy Processing Handbook, ch. 18 Milk and whey fractionation

sources.text: The cream-to-butter steps and the whey-cream remark are from Agroscope; the whey cream (25–30 % fat) and its use for butter from Tetra Pak. Neither gives parameters for whey cream alone, so those are the general ones for butter cream.
